scope.surface: Right-panel file detail toolbar, breadcrumb, editable source surface, persistent explorer, single file tab, and second-file selection

productLoss: Before the repair, Web rendered one file tab with a 283px editor beside a persistent 255px explorer. Lynx rendered an additional Files tab, a full-width editor, no explorer, and a permanent 28px Saved bar.
Lynx-for-Web also collapsed the file-detail subtree before Browser Preview compatibility supplied explicit column, toolbar, editor, and explorer allocation.

The structural repair does not close the remaining material gap: Web uses a guttered syntax-highlighted editor while Lynx uses a plain editable textarea. The current full-frame material residual remains explicitly measured.
harnessMismatch: The first discovery run was rejected because the live Browser Preview bridge blocked readProjectFile; listProjectEntries was available but file contents could not reach the Lynx pane.

The Web Pierre tree row did not react to outer CDP pointer dispatch even at the measured row center. The retained Web path records one failed pointer attempt and a composed-shadow-tree DOM click fallback; Lynx-for-Web and Native use real pointer or touch input.
Early detail captures were rejected because file-detail readiness reused the Files-browser activeKind=files gate after the product correctly transitioned to activeKind=file.
A proposed nested-text syntax preview rendered as zero-height columns in Lynx-for-Web and was reverted. It contributes no product or ledger improvement.
intentionalPlatformDelta: Native uses a textarea kernel rather than the Web Pierre DOM/Worker editor island. Editing remains functional, but syntax highlighting, gutter utilities, and line selection are not claimed equivalent.
acceptedRenderingNoise: One-pixel editor/explorer allocation quantization is accepted by the strict geometry gate.
Web and Lynx breadcrumb internals use different scroll primitives; the outer 539x40 toolbar and file identity are the comparable contract.
classification.evidenceBoundary: Browser before and after use one immutable snapshot, route, selected thread, dark theme, 1280x820 viewport, Web authority bundle, target files, and clean console. Exact-bundle Native independently proves the final single-tab editor/explorer structure and real file switching. Browser material pixels remain an explicit residual; Native material is not inferred.

material.reason: The initial Lynx-for-Web textarea attribute was not synchronized to its rendered value property, so the before pixel frame is not admitted as a product material measurement.

material.remainingDifference: Web retains syntax highlighting, line gutter, and richer editor primitives; Lynx retains a plain editable textarea.

materialAfter.behavior: Native-safe gutter and coarse Markdown token colors render by default; tapping the preview enters the real editable textarea.

fidelityImpact.modelChange: Add file-editor-detail as state 48 with Lynx and Native clients.

remainingRisk: The Native-safe preview reduces the measured material residual but remains coarser than the Web Pierre editor; per-token syntax coverage, gutter utilities, and line selection remain open rather than hidden.
Web tree opening required a composed-shadow-tree DOM click fallback after a measured CDP pointer did not activate Pierre selection; this is classified as harness input mismatch.
Native physical keyboard editing, selection, and save confirmation remain pending-user-session.
